facts.text: Using the existing warning system's field history as a reference means using years of recorded operation to validate simulation inputs and selected submodels, not the new closed-loop braking chain, subject to exposure, censored open-loop history and changed-system-boundary limitations.
facts.quote: The years of recorded operation of the current warning system can validate the simulation's inputs and some of its submodels, but not the new closed-loop braking chain, and only if three traps are respected.

facts.text: The manufacturer's warning systems have logged detections, warnings and operating conditions for years.
facts.quote: The manufacturer's warning systems have logged detections, warnings and conditions for years.

facts.text: Aviation accepts service history as evidence for similar systems when differences between the systems are justified.
facts.quote: aviation accepts service history for similar systems when differences are justified

facts.text: Replaying logged sensor data is common road-vehicle practice.
facts.quote: replaying logged sensor data is common road-vehicle practice

facts.text: European automated-vehicle rules require real-world data in the validation set.
facts.quote: the European automated-vehicle rules require real-world data in the validation set

facts.text: If the new braking system reuses the warning system's sensors and mounting, warning-system logs are direct validation data for those models, provided the logs contain usable ground truth.
facts.quote: If the new system reuses the warning system's sensors and mounting, the logs are direct validation data for those models, provided they hold usable ground truth.

facts.text: Warning-system field history can anchor the frequency and geometry of encountered objects, weather and site distributions, sensor contamination, nuisance-warning patterns and operator response timing.
facts.quote: The history can anchor the frequency and geometry of encountered objects, weather and site distributions, sensor contamination, nuisance-warning patterns and operator response timing

facts.text: Warning-system field history can serve as an independent replay set.
facts.quote: and serve as an independent replay set [Chapter 10].

facts.text: 'Proven in use' under ISO 26262-8 clause 14 and IEC 61508 is a route for reusing an element whose conditions of use match those of the fielded element.
facts.quote: "proven in use" (ISO 26262-8 clause 14, IEC 61508) is a route for reusing an element whose conditions of use match the fielded ones.

facts.text: The 'proven in use' route does not validate a simulator; adding automatic braking changes the item relative to the fielded warning system.
facts.quote: It does not validate a simulator, and adding automatic braking changes the item.

facts.text: No standard or assessor statement accepting a legacy system's history as the reference for validating a simulator was found.
facts.quote: No standard or assessor statement accepting a legacy system's history as the reference for validating a simulator was found [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Exposure must be known when using warning-system field history: 'few incidents in ten million hours' says little without the number of relevant encounters.
facts.quote: Exposure must be known: "few incidents in ten million hours" says little without the number of relevant encounters.

facts.text: Warning-system field history is censored and open-loop because warnings may cause operators to brake; logs rarely show what would have happened without intervention or how the machine and operator behave once automatic braking intervenes.
facts.quote: Field history is censored and open-loop: a warning may cause the operator to brake, so the logs rarely show what would have happened without intervention, or how machine and operator behave once braking intervenes.

facts.text: Changing from a warning product to automatic braking changes the system boundary: the warning product has no field evidence for brake command timing, pressure build-up, stability during intervention or unintended-braking hazards.
facts.quote: the warning product has no field evidence for brake command timing, pressure build-up, stability during intervention or unintended-braking hazards [Chapter 10].

facts.text: The defensible program claim is that warning-system field history validates selected simulation inputs and submodels and supports a representative scenario distribution, not that the history validates the automatic-braking simulator or braking function.
facts.quote: The defensible claim is that field history validates selected inputs and submodels and supports the representativeness of the scenario distribution, not that it validates the automatic-braking simulator [Chapter 10].
